subject: spanish
summary: Spanish is the cleanest of the four: questions are short, the reading passages attached are the right ones, multiple-choice listening items use proper tappable option boxes, and most schemes are one to three short tickable points. The faults are mainly in how the scheme rows are written. Several acceptable answers are sometimes merged into one tick box with slashes, so a 'give two details' question cannot be self-marked; examiner dot leaders and tick marks are left in the answers; and the first answer row often carries a paragraph of general exam rules. The two written-production cards show the mark ladder as a block of grey text followed by five empty 'First turn / First point' pickers, and the dialogue card is a very long phone scroll. Every listening card shows 'The embedded recording could not be loaded'.

issues.title: Alternative answers merged into one tick box
issues.detail: The question asks for two details, but the scheme is a single row worth all 5 marks: 'She is a singer / she represented Spain / she composed her song in English / she was not successful / she chose and international style.' A student cannot tick the two they gave or see how the 5 marks divide. It also carries a typo ('chose and international style'). Card 5 shows the right pattern for the same kind of question ('Any 2 of these - 2 marks each' with one row per point).
issues.suggested_fix: One row per acceptable detail under an 'Any 2 of these' heading with the mark for each, as on card 5.

issues.title: General exam rules pasted into the first answer row
issues.detail: The first tick row of many cards carries small grey boilerplate under the answer. On card 7 the answer 'Más de un millón.' is followed by eleven lines on the phone ('For the whole question the scheme prints: All answers must be in Spanish. Transcription ... is acceptable ... A forward slash indicates a choice of possible answers.Award 5 or 0 marks unless otherwise stated.'). Cards 6, 10 and 11 repeat 'All answers must be in English. If the entire listening comprehension test is answered in Spanish: mark as per Marking Scheme and award half of the marks gained.' On card 11 it sits under 'Concerts' only, making the first of three equal rows look different.
issues.suggested_fix: Move the language rule to one short line under the scheme heading (or the collapsed rules panel), outside the answer rows.

issues.title: Examiner marks left in answers
issues.detail: Card 3's answer reads '√ 91 6895360': a square-root sign standing for a tick, and the number without the spacing used in the options ('91 689 53 60'), so it is hard to match. Card 10's answer is '(√) parking'. Card 4's answer is '...... I had been looking at the horizon waiting for the planes .....' with dot leaders on both sides.
issues.suggested_fix: Strip the tick and dot leaders, print the answer exactly as the option is shown, and highlight the correct option in the question after the reveal.

issues.title: Written-production scheme is a text block plus empty pickers
issues.detail: The mark ladder is printed as a run of grey lines ('5 marks: Communicative intention fulfilled. / Good level of vocabulary. Verbs correct. / 3 - 4 marks: ...') mixed with examiner instructions ('Six turns. Five to be answered. If all turns are answered, mark all and award marks for the highest scoring FIVE', 'Guidelines as for Question 1 (a).]', 'Question 1. When marking this question, the priorities indicated for Content and Language in Section B, Q.5. should be broadly adhered to'). Below it are five sections titled 'First turn' / 'First point' with nothing but mark buttons, so the student scrolls back up to the ladder for each. More examiner rules follow the total ('TOTAL MARKS: 50 Candidates are required to attempt:- Either 1 (a) or 1 (b) AND Either 2 (a) or 2 (b)').
issues.suggested_fix: Show the ladder once as a small table (marks / what it looks like), and label each picker with the actual turn or point from the question. Drop the cross-references to other questions.

issues.title: Dialogue question is long and flat on the phone
issues.detail: The six Señora/Tú exchanges are printed as plain consecutive lines in the same serif type, with no visual difference between what the Señora says and the English instruction for the student's turn. On the phone the question alone is more than two screens before the answer box, and the attachment button sits after all of it. The header lists all four options of the section ('Question 1 (a) Dialogue Construction OR Question 1 (b) Letter OR ...').
issues.suggested_fix: Format as a dialogue: speaker label in bold or a left column, the Señora's Spanish lines distinct from the 'Tú' prompts, numbered turns that match the scheme's pickers.

issues.title: Small leftovers in question text
issues.detail: Card 7's question ends with '(1)', the paragraph reference, which reads like a mark or a stray number; the header also keeps 'Attempt all parts, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5.' Card 12's scheme awards 4, 3 and 3 marks to three equal examples with no explanation. Card 8's scheme repeats the answer as heading and as two rows. Listening headers run the Spanish title into the instruction in capitals. Reading attachments open at the top of the section, so the student scrolls past instructions (and on card 1 the page continues into sibling questions (a)-(f) below the passage).
issues.suggested_fix: Write '(paragraph 1)', drop the 'Attempt all parts' line, and note that the first correct example earns 4 marks.

issues.title: Listening audio not loading, no question page
issues.detail: All five listening cards show a 0:00 / 0:00 player with 'The embedded recording could not be loaded. Open the SEC recording.' (possibly a capture-environment fault). None has an attached page, which is fine since the question is fully typed.
issues.suggested_fix: Check the audio embed on a real device.
